title: Example: save a note with Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter
summary: An example plan showing what the format can do. It adds a keyboard shortcut for saving notes: **Cmd+Enter** on Mac, **Ctrl+Enter** on Windows and Linux. Pressing **Enter** on its own still starts a new line.

setup.title: Open the app
setup.body: Open the link above in a desktop browser (Chrome, Edge, Firefox or Safari).

setup.title: Sign in
setup.body: Choose **Sign in** at the bottom of the sidebar and enter an email address you can check. Type the code from the email to finish signing in.

setup.title: Go to a chapter
setup.body: Open **John 3** from the book picker. The tests below use this chapter.

sections.title: Saving with the keyboard
sections.intro: These tests check the new shortcut.

tests.title: Cmd+Enter or Ctrl+Enter saves the note
tests.why: This is the main change in the pull request.
expected: A note icon appears next to verse 16.

tests.title: Enter on its own still adds a new line
steps: Open the note on verse 16 again.
Click at the end of the text and press **Enter**, then type `second line`.
expected: `second line` appears on its own line under the first.

sections.title: Things that should not have changed

tests.title: The Save button still works
tests.before: You need the note from the first test.
steps: Open the note on verse 16 and click **Save**.
expected: The note box closes and the text you typed is kept.

notCovered: The code that detects Mac vs. Windows keyboards is covered by automated tests.
